title: Emergency and Critical Care
publisher: Cornell University College of Veterinary Medicine
topic: veterinary emergencies and urgent warning signs
geographicScope: The clinical service details are specific to Cornell in New York; the warning signs support general emergency awareness. PetPal users should use their nearest local emergency veterinary service.
content:
A pet with a life-threatening problem should be taken immediately to the nearest emergency veterinary clinic. Emergency teams evaluate and stabilize severely injured or critically ill animals; do not delay travel while waiting for online advice.

Warning signs listed by Cornell include unconsciousness or unresponsiveness, difficulty breathing, collapse, blue or pale gums, major trauma, excessive bleeding, difficulty urinating, unintended medication or toxin ingestion, seizure activity, severe or prolonged vomiting, non-productive retching, bloody diarrhea, and a bloated or painful abdomen.

At an emergency hospital, triage commonly begins with a brief history and baseline vital measurements. An unstable pet may be moved promptly for evaluation, diagnostic testing, and stabilization before a full consultation with the owner.
